child_briefs.title: Reachability primitive: check_wired over the import graph
child_briefs.scope: Build ONE new, pure/stdlib-only, single-file whole-file module harness/wire_up.py that decides whether a module is WIRED (reachable from a live entrypoint) without spawning a process or making any model/API/network/un-injected-subprocess call. Expose check_wired(repo_root, new_module_rel, *, roots=LIVE_ROOTS, exclude=()) -> WireResult(wired: bool, importers: list[str], reason: str, fix_hint: str): build the intra-project import graph by WRAPPING harness.rebuild.discover.module_import_graph (which AST-walks the full tree and so already captures function-local imports) over the non-test module list from discover.discover_modules; BFS from the declared LIVE_ROOTS frontier never traversing into a test/oracle module; the new module is WIRED iff at least one module in the reachable set imports it AFTER excluding the module's own oracle from the importer set; hard-fail (wired=False) on zero live importers; soft-warn (wired=True with a warn reason) on imported-but-uncalled; and supplement with a config/** grep for the module/symbol so dynamically-registered wiring is not mis-flagged as orphan. Declare LIVE_ROOTS (orchestrator, orchestrator_worker, autowork_daemon, planner.cli, the claude/gemini hook entrypoints, webui_control, the overseer/services entrypoints) here as a module constant. Author the hand-written RED oracle tests/harness/test_wire_up.py as the verification_command target.
child_briefs.non_goals: Do NOT add the accept-path call, the gates.py/gate_runner.py gate, the procedure.py phase, or the plan_validator violation — those are separate dependent leaves. Do NOT reimplement discover.module_import_graph or re-parse imports — wrap it. No new agent spawns, model/API/network/SSE calls, or un-injected subprocesses; the root set, import graph, and filesystem reads are injected/stdlib so the oracle drives them hermetically. No changes to harness/orchestrator.py or the autowork daemon in THIS leaf. The word 'integration' is out of scope here: this is a NEW single-file whole-file module, not an existing-symbol edit. This is the ONE leaf whose oracle may be isolated (it tests a pure primitive); its reachability is established by the dependent accept-gate leaf and the dogfood acceptance, not here.
child_briefs.inputs: harness.rebuild.discover.discover_modules(source_root) -> (modules, tests, seeds) and harness.rebuild.discover.module_import_graph(source_root, modules) -> dict[str, set[str]] as fixed read-only seams. The repo tree layout (intra-project module naming) as observed by discover. The set of real live entrypoints to seed the BFS (LIVE_ROOTS, declared in this module).
child_briefs.deliverables: harness/wire_up.py exposing WireResult(wired: bool, importers: list[str], reason: str, fix_hint: str), the LIVE_ROOTS constant, and check_wired(repo_root, new_module_rel, *, roots=LIVE_ROOTS, exclude=()) -> WireResult implemented over discover's import graph with BFS-from-roots, own-oracle exclusion, zero-importer hard-fail, imported-but-uncalled soft-warn, and a config/** grep supplement. The RED oracle tests/harness/test_wire_up.py named as the leaf verification_command python -m pytest tests/harness/test_wire_up.py -q.
child_briefs.interfaces: WireResult(wired: bool, importers: list[str], reason: str, fix_hint: str); LIVE_ROOTS: list[str]; check_wired(repo_root, new_module_rel, *, roots=LIVE_ROOTS, exclude=()) -> WireResult. Consumes discover.discover_modules and discover.module_import_graph without modifying them.

child_briefs.title: Accept-time wire-up gate in _auto_commit_accepted (flag-gated)
child_briefs.scope: Additively EDIT the existing symbol harness/orchestrator.py::_auto_commit_accepted to enforce reachability at the single convergent accept chokepoint, behind the default-OFF flag autowork.wire_up_gate. Insert the gate at the post-mutation / pre-merge point (after the mutation-gate arm, before git_integration.merge_staging_to_parent): when the flag is ON and the candidate created a NEW live module, call wire_up.check_wired(working_dir, <new module rel>); on ORPHAN (wired=False) reject by REUSING the existing rejection machinery exactly as the mutation gate does — _rollback_rejected_commit(staging_path, result.get('sha'), target_rel, task_id, 'orphan_unwired') + git_integration.remove_staging_worktree(str(staging_path), parent_root=worktree_root) + _mark_blocked(state_dir, task_id, outcome='orphan_unwired') + return False, emitting the failure via the existing ledger / _emit_gate_failure pattern; on WIRED proceed to the merge unchanged. Preserve every existing accept behaviour and passing test; the gate is a no-op when the flag is OFF or the candidate created no new module. Author the EDGE-ASSERTING RED oracle tests/harness/test_wire_up_accept_gate.py.
child_briefs.non_goals: Do NOT author harness/wire_up.py (consume it) or the gates.py/procedure.py/plan_validator changes. No new agent spawns, model/API/network/SSE calls, or un-injected subprocesses. This is an EXISTING-symbol additive integration that preserves all current behaviour and tests, editing exactly ONE file. The flag autowork.wire_up_gate ships default-OFF and is NOT flipped here; flipping is gated on the dogfood acceptance with owner sign-off. The trap: this leaf adds a CALL SITE, so its oracle MUST assert the edge fired (spy on check_wired + drive the live accept path with an orphan), not merely that check_wired works in isolation.
child_briefs.inputs: From wire-up-primitive: check_wired(repo_root, new_module_rel, *, roots, exclude) -> WireResult and WireResult. The ALREADY-BUILT accept chokepoint _auto_commit_accepted and its rejection machinery _rollback_rejected_commit(worktree_root, sha, target_rel, task_id, kind), git_integration.remove_staging_worktree(path, *, parent_root), _mark_blocked(state_dir, task_id, *, outcome), the impl_progress.jsonl ledger writer, and the flag-reading helper for autowork.* config flags.
child_briefs.deliverables: Edited harness/orchestrator.py whose _auto_commit_accepted, when autowork.wire_up_gate is ON and a new module was created, runs check_wired between the mutation gate and the merge, rolls back + blocks an orphan via the existing machinery with outcome 'orphan_unwired', and is a no-op otherwise. The EDGE-ASSERTING RED oracle tests/harness/test_wire_up_accept_gate.py (spy asserts the live accept path called check_wired and an orphan candidate was blocked; a wired candidate merges) named as the leaf verification_command python -m pytest tests/harness/test_wire_up_accept_gate.py -q.
child_briefs.interfaces: Consumes check_wired(repo_root, new_module_rel, *, roots, exclude) -> WireResult. Edits _auto_commit_accepted(state_dir, task, task_id) -> bool additively, preserving its signature and all existing accept/reject behaviour, adding only a flag-gated orphan-rejection arm.

child_briefs.title: wired GateResult function + gate_runner dispatch label
child_briefs.scope: Additively EDIT overseer/gates.py to add a pure wired(report) -> GateResult that returns ok=False (with a reason/fix_hint pointing at the orphan) when report's live_importers count is zero and ok=True otherwise, exporting it via __all__. Additively EDIT overseer/gate_runner.py::_run_gate to add a 'wired' label branch mapping to gates.wired over the importer-count report seam (read from procedure_artifacts, e.g. arts.get('wire_report')), consistent with the existing label branches, and extend gate_label_for as needed so the dispatch (mode, phase) -> 'wired' label resolves. Preserve every existing gate and passing test. Author the RED oracle tests/overseer/test_wired_gate.py.
child_briefs.non_goals: Do NOT add the WIRE_UP phase to PROCEDURE_REGISTRY (that is the dependent wire-up-fsm-phase leaf) and do NOT author harness/wire_up.py or the accept-gate edit. No new agent spawns, model/API/network/SSE calls, or un-injected subprocesses; wired() is pure over its report argument. EXISTING-symbol additive integration preserving all current behaviour and tests. The trap: the oracle MUST assert gate_runner DISPATCHES the 'wired' label to gates.wired (the wiring edge between dispatch and gate), not merely that wired() works standalone.
child_briefs.inputs: From overseer/gates.py: GateResult(ok: bool, reason: str, fix_hint: str). From overseer/gate_runner.py: the _run_gate(label, arts, attested, sd) -> GateResult dispatch structure and gate_label_for(mode, phase) -> Optional[str]. The shape of the wire report (a mapping carrying live_importers) produced for a dispatch task.
child_briefs.deliverables: Edited overseer/gates.py exposing wired(report) -> GateResult (zero live_importers => not-ok) in __all__. Edited overseer/gate_runner.py whose _run_gate handles the 'wired' label by calling gates.wired over the report seam, with gate_label_for resolving the WIRE_UP phase to 'wired'. The RED oracle tests/overseer/test_wired_gate.py asserting the dispatch edge (gate_runner routes 'wired' to gates.wired) and the zero-importer => not-ok behaviour, named as python -m pytest tests/overseer/test_wired_gate.py -q.
child_briefs.interfaces: wired(report) -> GateResult; _run_gate label 'wired' -> gates.wired over the report seam; gate_label_for(mode, phase) resolving the WIRE_UP phase to the 'wired' label. Preserves GateResult and all existing gate-runner labels.

child_briefs.title: WIRE_UP phase between VERIFY and RESTORE in the dispatch procedure
child_briefs.scope: Additively EDIT overseer/procedure.py to insert a new Phase('WIRE_UP', 'wired', <next-action string>) into PROCEDURE_REGISTRY['dispatch'].phases BETWEEN the existing VERIFY and RESTORE phases, so that because RESTORE's pass yields the terminal Complete (== DONE), DONE is unreachable until the wired gate passes. Change nothing in the pure reducer advance(...) — the new phase rides the existing reduce semantics (gate fail => Blocked, pass => next phase). Preserve every existing procedure, phase order, and passing test. Author the RED oracle tests/overseer/test_wire_up_phase.py.
child_briefs.non_goals: Do NOT author the wired gate function or the gate_runner branch (that is the wired-gate-fn dependency) and do NOT touch the accept-gate or plan_validator. No new agent spawns, model/API/network/SSE calls, or un-injected subprocesses; this is a pure registry edit. EXISTING-symbol additive integration preserving all current behaviour and tests, editing exactly ONE file. The trap: the oracle MUST assert the FSM wiring — that PROCEDURE_REGISTRY['dispatch'] contains WIRE_UP ordered before RESTORE AND that advance returns Blocked on a zero-importer wired GateResult — not an isolated dataclass construction test.
child_briefs.inputs: From overseer/procedure.py: Phase(name, gate, next_action), Procedure(mode, phases), PROCEDURE_REGISTRY with the existing dispatch order PREFLIGHT->STAGE->BUILD->VERIFY->RESTORE, and advance(procedure, phase, gate_result) -> Decision (next phase | Blocked | Complete). From wired-gate-fn: the 'wired' gate label that the new phase binds.
child_briefs.deliverables: Edited overseer/procedure.py whose PROCEDURE_REGISTRY['dispatch'] phase list is PREFLIGHT->STAGE->BUILD->VERIFY->WIRE_UP->RESTORE, the WIRE_UP phase binding the 'wired' gate and a next-action string, with advance unchanged. The RED oracle tests/overseer/test_wire_up_phase.py asserting WIRE_UP is ordered before RESTORE and that advance returns Blocked on a zero-importer wired GateResult, named as python -m pytest tests/overseer/test_wire_up_phase.py -q.
child_briefs.interfaces: PROCEDURE_REGISTRY['dispatch'] gains a WIRE_UP phase (gate 'wired') between VERIFY and RESTORE; advance(procedure, phase, gate_result) -> Decision is consumed unchanged.

child_briefs.title: missing_wiring_oracle plan-validation requirement
child_briefs.scope: Additively EDIT harness/planner/plan_validator.py to require that a leaf creating a NEW module declares a WIRING oracle, rejecting it pre-spawn otherwise. Add an _is_wiring_oracle(test_path_or_source) classifier (a test that imports a live entrypoint which is NOT the leaf module and NOT under tests/, carries a test_*_wired / registers / invokes marker, and does NOT mock the seam) and emit a 'missing_wiring_oracle' violation for any new-module / test_authoring leaf whose declared tests contain no such oracle. Preserve every existing per-task validation and passing test. Author the RED oracle tests/planner/test_missing_wiring_oracle.py.
child_briefs.non_goals: Do NOT author harness/wire_up.py, the accept gate, the gates.py/gate_runner.py change, or the procedure.py phase. Do NOT reimplement the existing plan validator — add the violation beside the existing checks. No new agent spawns, model/API/network/SSE calls, or un-injected subprocesses. EXISTING-symbol additive integration preserving all current behaviour and tests, editing exactly ONE file. This leaf is independent of the others (no dependency) and may build in parallel.
child_briefs.inputs: From harness/planner/plan_validator.py: the existing per-task validation entrypoint and its violation-collection structure, the task/leaf schema (meta_task_type, declared test paths, mutation_target). The definition of a wiring oracle from the epic THE TRAP section.
child_briefs.deliverables: Edited harness/planner/plan_validator.py exposing an _is_wiring_oracle classifier and emitting a 'missing_wiring_oracle' violation for a new-module leaf lacking a wiring oracle, beside the existing checks. The RED oracle tests/planner/test_missing_wiring_oracle.py asserting a new-module leaf without a wiring oracle is rejected and one with it passes, named as python -m pytest tests/planner/test_missing_wiring_oracle.py -q.
child_briefs.interfaces: _is_wiring_oracle(...) -> bool classifier and a 'missing_wiring_oracle' violation added to the existing plan-validation flow, preserving its signature and all current violations.
